issues.legal_issue: The redetermination mechanism available for certain land acquisitions does not apply to acquisitions governed by a separate requisitioning and acquisition statute.
material_facts: The land was first requisitioned under a defence law and later acquired, with residual acquisition matters governed by a separate statute.
The landowners agreed to compensation under the separate statute and later sought redetermination based on a higher arbitral award for other acquired land.
The governing statute provided its own compensation principles and procedures, distinct from those in the general land acquisition statute.
issues.conclusion: The statutory redetermination mechanism in Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act does not apply to acquisitions under the separate statute, including the acquisition proceedings carried over from the defence law.
issues.legal_principle: The separate statute is a self-contained code with its own compensation criteria and procedure, so the Land Acquisition Act is not incorporated into it by implication. Section 8, including its agreement and arbitration procedures and its market-value measure for acquisition, differs from the Land Acquisition Act's compensation provisions. The Court applied Union of India v. Hari Krishan Khosla, Union of India v. Gurbachan Singh, Union of India v. Babu Singh, and Union of India v. Dhanwanti Devi. It distinguished Haji Mohammad Ekramul Haq because the separate statute had since been amended, and distinguished Nagpur Improvement Trust and U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad because those statutes incorporated the Land Acquisition Act's compensation provisions.

predicates.separate_requisition_acquisition_proceed: The property was requisitioned or acquired through a proceeding governed by a separate requisitioning and acquisition framework.
predicates.compensation_framework_is_self_contained: The governing framework set out its own criteria and procedures for determining compensation.
predicates.claimant_seeks_redetermination_under_gen: The claimant sought to use a redetermination route provided by the general land acquisition framework.

issues.definition: When a separate requisition and acquisition proceeding has its own complete compensation framework and the claimant seeks redetermination through the general acquisition route, that route is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: A landowner who agreed to compensation cannot compel the acquiring authority to reopen the agreement solely because a later award grants higher compensation for similar land.
material_facts: The landowners entered into agreements fixing compensation for their acquired land.
They relied on a later arbitral award granting higher compensation for other land and sought a fresh agreement or reopening of the compensation settlement.
There was no finding that the agreements were vitiated by fraud, misrepresentation, or a similar defect, and no express statutory right to reopen them.
issues.conclusion: The landowners had no enforceable right to compel the acquiring authority to reopen their agreements on the basis of the later award.
issues.legal_principle: An agreement fixing compensation is ordinarily binding unless vitiated, and changing it requires the parties' agreement. A substantive right to reopen a final compensation determination must be expressly provided by statute and cannot be implied; an unavailable statutory remedy cannot be achieved indirectly. The Court relied on Union of India v. Filip Tiago De Gama of Vedem Vasco De Gama, Bhavnagar University v. Palitana Sugar Mill, and Unique Butyle Tube Industries v. U.P. Financial Corporation for the principle that clear statutory language cannot be enlarged by implication.

rule.if: proceeding_to_compel_reopening_of_compensation_agreement and compensation_was_agreed and later_comparable_award_exists and no_agreement_vitiation_is_established and no_express_reopening_right_exists

predicates.proceeding_to_compel_reopening_of_compen: The claimant asked a court to require the acquiring authority to reopen an agreed compensation settlement.
predicates.compensation_was_agreed: The claimant and acquiring authority had agreed on the compensation for the property.
predicates.later_comparable_award_exists: A later award fixed higher compensation for other land said to be comparable.
predicates.no_agreement_vitiation_is_established: No fraud, misrepresentation, or other defect vitiating the agreement was established.
predicates.no_express_reopening_right_exists: The governing law did not expressly give the claimant a right to reopen the agreed determination.

issues.definition: When compensation was agreed, a later comparable award exists, no defect in the agreement is established, and no express reopening right exists, reopening cannot be compelled.

issues.legal_issue: The government may challenge in court a compensation award made by a statutory officer who reopened a concluded matter without authority.
material_facts: A statutory land-acquisition officer issued a supplementary compensation award after reopening a concluded compensation matter.
The government challenged the supplementary award on the ground that the officer had used a redetermination mechanism unavailable under the governing acquisition framework.
The officer's authority was limited to the powers conferred by the governing law.
issues.conclusion: The government was a person aggrieved and could maintain a writ petition challenging the officer's award as made without jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: A statutory officer must act within the powers conferred by law. An order made by invoking an inapplicable legal mechanism and thereby exceeding those powers may be challenged as a jurisdictional nullity by the government.

predicates.government_challenges_compensation_award: The government brought a writ proceeding to challenge a compensation award.
predicates.statutory_officer_reopened_concluded_mat: A statutory officer reopened a compensation matter that had already been concluded.
predicates.officer_exceeded_conferred_authority: The officer acted beyond the powers conferred by the governing law.

issues.definition: When the government challenges an award in a writ proceeding and a statutory officer reopened a concluded matter beyond the officer's powers, the government may maintain the challenge.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court should not set aside a writ court's decision solely for delay when the writ court exercised its discretion to entertain the case and its decision is legally sustainable.
material_facts: The government filed its writ petition after a substantial delay.
The writ court nevertheless exercised its discretion to entertain the petition and set aside the supplementary award.
The appellate court found the writ court's decision legally sustainable.
issues.conclusion: The delay alone did not justify setting aside the writ court's decision on appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Delay and laches are primarily matters for the writ court to assess. Once that court has exercised its jurisdiction despite delay, an appellate court should not reverse its decision on delay alone where the decision is legally sustainable.

predicates.appeal_from_writ_court_decision: A party appealed from a writ court's decision.
predicates.writ_court_entertained_case_despite_dela: The writ court exercised its discretion to hear the case although it had been filed after delay.
predicates.decision_is_legally_sustainable: The writ court's decision is legally sustainable.

issues.definition: When a writ court entertains a delayed case and its decision is legally sustainable, an appellate court does not reverse that decision for delay alone.
